# Stylistic Text Generator Comparator

[![Built with askThili](https://ask.thili.ai/api/v1/public/projects/tsk5up2p4e/badge.svg)](https://ask.thili.ai/b/tsk5up2p4e)

This project, the "Stylistic Text Generator Comparator," is designed for sports journalists. It provides a way to compare sports commentary text generated by a LoRA-adapted Language Model with an N-gram model, both fine-tuned on specific sports commentary styles.

## What you are building

**Goal.** You will build a tool that allows sports journalists to compare text generated by an N-gram model and a LoRA-adapted LLM, both fine-tuned on specific sports commentary styles.

**Done when.** Your project is complete when you have successfully fine-tuned a pre-trained LLM with a LoRA adapter on a custom sports commentary text style and can qualitatively compare its text generation quality against an N-gram model built from the same text.

## Milestones

Tick these off as you go, and commit after each one.

- [x] **1. Prepare a small corpus of sports commentary text.**  
      Hint: Data preprocessing
- [x] **2. Implement the n-gram model and generate text from it.**  
      Hint: N-gram modeling
- [x] **3. Load a small pre-trained LLM and implement LoRA adapter injection.**  
      Hint: LoRA adapter injection
- [x] **4. Fine-tune the LoRA adapter on the sports commentary corpus.**  
      Hint: LoRA adapter training
- [x] **5. Generate text from the LoRA-adapted LLM.**  
      Hint: Text generation
- [x] **6. Provide a qualitative comparison interface for generated texts from both models.**  
      Hint: Text comparison

## Run it

You need Python 3.11+ and git.

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Check the CLI is wired up
python -m app.cli hello

# Prepare & inspect the corpus
python -m app.cli corpus

# Generate with the N-gram model
python -m app.cli ngram --prompt "The goalkeeper" --tokens 30

# Generate with the LoRA-adapted LLM (trains first; takes ~15s)
python -m app.cli generate --prompt "What an absolute thunderbolt" --epochs 15

# Full side-by-side comparison
python -m app.cli compare --prompt "The striker" --epochs 15

# Run the full test suite
pytest
```

Your work lives in `app/` and `tests/`. The key modules are:
- [`app/corpus.py`](app/corpus.py) — corpus preparation & vocabulary
- [`app/ngram.py`](app/ngram.py) — N-gram model with backoff & perplexity
- [`app/model.py`](app/model.py) — small causal Transformer LM
- [`app/lora.py`](app/lora.py) — LoRA layer injection
- [`app/trainer.py`](app/trainer.py) — LoRA fine-tuning loop
- [`app/generator.py`](app/generator.py) — LLM text generation
- [`app/comparator.py`](app/comparator.py) — side-by-side comparison & report
- [`app/core.py`](app/core.py) — `milestone_1()` through `milestone_6()` stubs (all implemented)
- [`tests/test_core.py`](tests/test_core.py) — one test per milestone

## Settings and secrets

Model settings live in `.env`, which is ignored by git. **Never commit `.env` or paste a key into code.** If a key ever
reaches GitHub, treat it as leaked and make a new one.

## Stretch ideas

- Allow users to input a short prompt to guide the text generation from both models.
- Implement a simple quantitative metric (e.g., perplexity) to provide an objective measure alongside the qualitative comparison.
- Experiment with different LoRA ranks or training parameters to observe their impact on the generated text's style and coherence.
